# Mercury Composable

> A Java framework for building composable, event-driven applications from self-contained
> functions wired by YAML event flows. Functions couple only through named routes and event
> envelopes, so orchestration is configuration, not code. It runs on Java 21 virtual threads
> (synchronous RPC performs like reactive) and ascends three layers: an event-driven core
> (Platform Core), composable orchestration (Event Script), and a semantic layer where an
> Active Knowledge Graph *is* the application.

> This file is the machine-readable map of the documentation, organized by layer, to help an
> AI agent (or a human) jump directly to the right page.

## Start here
- [Home](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/): the three-layer model and where to go next.
- [Getting Started](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/getting-started/): a working app in five minutes (quickstart), then how a request flows through flows, functions, and REST.
- [AI Developer Guide](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/ai-developer-guide/): **start here if you are an AI agent** — brownfield orientation, layer-choice decision tree, adding features, testing, and pointers to each layer's DSL guide.

## Layer 1 — Event-driven foundation (Platform Core)
- [Architecture Overview](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/architecture/): layers, components, the in-memory event bus, threading, core APIs.
- [Methodology](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/methodology/): the four composable design principles.
- [Event-driven Foundation](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-driven/): Layer 1 overview — functions, route names, PostOffice, EventEnvelope, the in-memory event bus.
- [Write your first function](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-driven/write-your-first-function/): step-by-step — define a function, expose it over HTTP, call it via PostOffice, test it.
- [Function Execution Strategies](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-driven/function-execution/): virtual vs. kernel threads, Mono/Flux.
- [Function AI agent guide](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-driven/ai-agent-guide/): @PreLoad annotation contract, TypedLambdaFunction interface, pre-write checklist, PostOffice patterns — for deterministic function generation.
- [REST Automation](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/rest-automation/): declare HTTP endpoints via rest.yaml, no controllers.
- [REST AI agent guide](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/rest-automation/ai-agent-guide/): the authoritative context for authoring rest.yaml deterministically — structure, binding modes, a pre-write checklist, and a worked example.
- [REST grammar](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/rest-automation/rest-grammar/): the rule-based reference for the rest.yaml DSL — how an endpoint maps to a service or a flow, plus the CORS and header-transform blocks.
- [rest-automation.json](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/rest-automation/rest-automation.json): the machine-readable rest.yaml catalog — entry fields, http methods, binding modes, cors/headers blocks, invariants.

## Layer 2 — Composable orchestration (Event Script)
- [Composable Orchestration (Overview)](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-script/): Layer 2 overview — what Event Script is, the flow mental model, where it sits.
- [Event Script Syntax](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-script/syntax/): the flow DSL — structure, task types, data mapping, Simple Plugins (`f:` functions).
- [Flow AI agent guide](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-script/ai-agent-guide/): authoring flows deterministically — compile contract, pre-write checklist, recipe, worked examples.
- [Flow grammar](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-script/flow-grammar/): the rules — flow structure, task fields, the eight execution types, the data-mapping mini-language.
- [event-script-flow.json](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-script/event-script-flow.json): the machine-readable flow schema; ingest and validate against it.
- [Flow Configuration Schema](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/flow-schema-reference/): precise flow YAML field reference.
- [Build, Test and Deploy](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/build-test-deploy/): entry point, unit tests, packaging.

## Layer 3 — Semantic (Active Knowledge Graph)
- [Knowledge Graph as Application](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/): the paradigm, execution model, node model, built-in skills, layer integration, Playground & AI companion, and maturity.
- [Minimalist Property Graph](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/property-graph/): the in-memory property-graph data model and API the layer builds on.
- [Build your first graph](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/build-your-first-graph/): hands-on walkthrough — model a service in the Playground, dry-run it, then deploy it and call it over REST without writing application code.
- [Workflow suspension](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/workflow-suspension/): express a long-running process as a sequence of short graph runs — suspend while waiting on a person or another system, persist state to a pluggable store, resume by business correlation id without re-executing completed steps.
- [Composing the layers](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/composing-the-layers/): how a graph reaches external APIs (data-dictionary + provider nodes), delegates to sub-graphs and Event Script flows (graph.extension), and is exposed as a REST endpoint through the graph-executor flow.
- [Playground & AI companion](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/playground-and-companion/): the interactive workbench for building, dry-running and inspecting graphs — its command grammar, collaborative sessions, and the companion endpoint that lets an AI co-author in a live session.

### Operating the MiniGraph Playground — start here if you are an AI agent
These are self-contained; you should not need the engine source or the tutorial walkthroughs:

- [AI agent guide](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/ai-agent-guide/): the companion-endpoint contract. Use the **synchronous** `POST /api/companion/{session-id}/sync` — it returns the command outcome **in-band** as `{ok, output, error, result}` (self-correct from `error`; no console relay needed) and tees the same output to the human's WebSocket console for real-time human+AI collaboration.
- [Command grammar](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/command-reference/): the rules — lexical, namespaces, the constant set (+ `f:` plugin / `$.` JSONPath source forms), every command's syntax (incl. `help {topic}` and the discovery commands `list graphs` / `list flows` / `describe graph {graph-id}`), node types, parallel fan-out/join traversal, the skill→property matrix, **Provider & Dictionary authoring** (the data-dictionary method), **iterative fetching** (`for_each` with guaranteed ordered aggregation), the **Island knowledge layer** (required — no node left unconnected), failure routing, and the `graph.math`/`graph.js` statement grammar.
- [minigraph-commands.json](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/minigraph-commands.json): the machine-readable command catalog; ingest it and validate commands against it before dispatching.
- [Built-in skills reference](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/knowledge-graph/skills-reference/): per-skill properties, gotchas, and examples.

## Operate & integrate
- [Observability](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/observability/): built-in distributed tracing across the three layers and OpenTelemetry/OTLP export (W3C trace context, the distributed.trace.forwarder hook, the opentelemetry-forwarder extension).
- [Spring Boot Integration](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/spring-boot/): run Mercury as a Spring Boot app.
- [Event over HTTP](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-over-http/): cross-instance event communication.
- [HTTP Response Streaming](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/http-streaming/): stream token segments and progress events over plain HTTP (SSE or chunked/NDJSON) — a callee sends events marked `x-event-stream: data|eof|exception` to the caller's reply route; declare the endpoint with `stream: true` in rest.yaml for ordered delivery; produce with EventStreamWriter.
- [Polyglot Functions](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/polyglot-functions/): write functions in Python or Node.js as Event-over-HTTP peers — official wrappers (docs: accenture.github.io/mercury-python, accenture.github.io/mercury-nodejs) with the engines' preload/envelope/actuator/log contracts; flows call them via yaml.event.over.http; graph.task requires engine v4.11.11+; orchestration stays on the engine (no flows/graphs in wrappers).
- [Minimalist Kafka](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/minimalist-kafka/): opt-in minimalist-kafka library — route Kafka topics into Event Script flows (kafka-flow-adapter.yaml: topic/flow/flows/group/partition/schema.enabled/serializer/ttl) and publish via simple.kafka.notification; second-level routing (flows rule list: input.header/input.body selectors, exact/wildcard/regex matchers, first match wins, flow:// or task:// targets, mandatory default), best-effort registry-less JSON decode (serializer: 'json'), externalized producer/consumer client templates, per-client opt-out for a one-way bridge leg (kafka.producer.enabled / kafka.consumer.enabled, default true; a dlq-topic without a producer fails startup; kafka.health falls back to the producer template when the consumer is off), per-binding consumer group, partition pinning, content-based partitioning (explicit partition header bypasses partitioners; SimpleRandomPartitioner default; template partitioner.class honored), bounded retry + per-topic dead-letter, continuous traceparent, and opt-in Confluent Schema Registry payloads (JSON Schema / Avro, id-driven via schema-id/schema-type headers).
- [Twin Kafka](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/twin-kafka/): opt-in twin-kafka library adding a SECOND Kafka cluster on top of minimalist-kafka — `secondary.kafka.notification` (publish), optional secondary flow adapter (`yaml.secondary.kafka.flow.adapter`), `secondary.kafka.health`; each the exact counterpart of its primary sibling on `secondary.*` keys (templates `secondary-kafka-producer.properties` / `secondary-kafka-consumer.properties`, overridable with `secondary.kafka.producer.properties` / `secondary.kafka.consumer.properties`; outbound `secondary.kafka.correlation.id.header` / `secondary.kafka.trace.id.header` / `secondary.kafka.traceparent.header` fall back to the primary globals; per-client opt-out `secondary.kafka.producer.enabled` / `secondary.kafka.consumer.enabled`, default true, for a one-way bridge leg). A bridge is just a flow — consume from one cluster's adapter, publish through the other's notification function — with trace and correlation-id continuity across both hops; dead letters return to the originating cluster. Schema Registry is optional PER CLUSTER (`secondary.schema.registry.url` + `secondary-schema-registry.properties`, its own schema-id cache), making the asymmetric on-prem-Apache-no-registry ⇄ cloud-Confluent-with-registry topology configuration-only; the bridge does NOT translate schema ids (unique only within one registry) — bridge framed payloads by decode/re-encode (`schema.enabled: true` inbound + `subject` header outbound), never relay raw framed bytes. Local dev: `kafka-standalone` with `dual.servers=true` runs both brokers (127.0.0.1:9092 + 127.0.0.1:8092); worked example in examples/twin-kafka-demo.
- [Schema Registry Mock](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/schema-registry-mock/): standalone, platform-core-only mock of the Confluent Schema Registry for local dev (helpers/schema-registry-standalone) — faithful REST API (GET /, POST /subjects/{subject}/versions, GET /schemas/ids/{id}), schema carried as an escaped string, global content-based ids, Confluent error_code bodies (40403/42201); worked example in examples/schema-registry-demo (curl + zero-dependency .mjs scripts).

- [Sync-over-Async](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/sync-over-async/): opt-in extension exposing synchronous REST request/response over an async cross-pod Kafka backend via a Redis return route keyed by correlation-id (sync.over.async.enabled, redis.* + sync.* config).
- [Minimalist Service Mesh](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/service-mesh/): Kafka-based service discovery and routing.

## Rust implementation
- [Mercury for Rust](https://github.com/Accenture/mercury): the official Rust implementation — same
  three layers, same flow YAML (flow files port unchanged), behavior-synced with this engine; its
  docs live at [accenture.github.io/mercury](https://accenture.github.io/mercury/) with its own
  llms.txt map. Building functions in Rust? Start there; the graph/flow DSLs are shared.

## Reference
- [API Overview](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/api-overview/): PostOffice, Platform, EventEnvelope, configuration APIs.
- [Annotations Reference](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/annotations-reference/): @PreLoad, @MainApplication, and the rest.
- [Configuration Reference](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/configuration-reference/): application.properties / application.yml keys.
- [Event Envelope Reference](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-envelope-reference/): the EventEnvelope and PostOffice API.
- [Event Envelope Wire Format](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/event-envelope-wire-format/): the language-neutral serialized envelope contract for Event over HTTP interop (self-contained spec — implement a new language port from this page alone).
- [Registration Metadata Contract](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/registration-metadata-contract/): the cross-language contract behind `@PreLoad` (ADR-0009) — one metadata model and fixed boot semantics, carried by per-language idioms (Java annotations, Rust macros), proven by shared golden vectors.
- [Reserved Names & Headers](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/reserved-names-and-headers/): system-reserved routes and headers.
- [Actuators & HTTP Client](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/actuators-and-http-client/): built-in actuator endpoints and the AsyncHttpRequest API.
- [Architecture Decision Records](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/arch-decisions/ADR/): the durable architecture decisions (decoupled functions, virtual-thread engine, Map/PoJo I/O, the three paradigm layers, one-atom-four-roles) with their rationale.
- [Code Conventions](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/code-conventions/): recommended code organization and naming — the `tasks` package for flow-task functions, route-naming discipline, function granularity.
- [Documentation Conventions](https://accenture.github.io/mercury-composable/guides/documentation-conventions/): the docs canon — *layer* means the three paradigm layers only, the function/service/task/skill vocabulary, the story spine, and the AI-discovery contract; CI-enforced by `scripts/check-doc-canon.py`.
